covers.quote: Use the correct term when referring to ambassadors, high commissioners, nuncios and other diplomatic staff.
The title for diplomats depends on what they represent:
High commissioners represent Commonwealth countries.
Ambassadors represent non-Commonwealth countries.
Nuncios represent the Holy See, the governing body of the Roman Catholic Church.

rules.quote: Use the correct term when referring to diplomats
rules.violation_condition: A diplomatic representative is given a title inconsistent with the entity represented: high commissioner for a Commonwealth country, ambassador for a non-Commonwealth country, or nuncio for the Holy See.
when: The represented country or body is identifiable.
Apply the three title distinctions stated on this page; do not infer additional distinctions for other diplomatic positions.
rules.why: G-2 combines the representation cases into one title-choice check; G-4 absorbs the introductory restatement. The heading has a distinct check beyond grouping its children.

covers.quote: Use initial capitals when writing to ambassadors, high commissioners and nuncios.
The pronouns ‘His’ and ‘Her’ are part of the title. Write these with an initial capital as well.

parts.quote: His Excellency Mr Babar Amin, High Commissioner for Pakistan

rules.quote: Use initial capitals for the titles of high commissioners, ambassadors and nuncios
rules.violation_condition: When writing to an ambassador, high commissioner or nuncio, a substantive word in the diplomat’s title has a lowercase initial, including ‘his’ or ‘her’ when it forms part of the title.
when: When writing to ambassadors, high commissioners and nuncios.
The pronouns ‘His’ and ‘Her’ are included when they form part of the title.
rules.why: G-4 combines the heading and body wording; the pronoun instruction extends the same title-capitalisation check rather than creating another finding.

covers.quote: Use ‘His Excellency’ or ‘Her Excellency’ to address high commissioners, ambassadors and nuncios.

parts.quote: Her Excellency the Hon Dame Annette Faye King, High Commissioner for New Zealand
Her Excellency Ms Francesca Tardioli, Ambassador of Italy
His Excellency Mr Tim Kane, Ambassador to Brazil
His Excellency Archbishop (Most Rev) Adolfo Tito Yllana, Apostolic Nuncio for Holy See

rules.quote: Address high commissioners, ambassadors and nuncios with ‘His Excellency’ or ‘Her Excellency’
rules.violation_condition: A high commissioner’s, ambassador’s or nuncio’s style of address accompanying their name omits ‘His Excellency’ or ‘Her Excellency’.
when: Applies to styles of address accompanying the names of high commissioners, ambassadors and nuncios.
Email and letter salutations follow the separate formal and informal opening requirements.
rules.why: G-4 treats the heading and body as one requirement; E-2 attaches the following examples to this address-form rule.

covers.quote: In formal correspondence with ambassadors, high commissioners and nuncios:
In informal correspondence:
Open with ‘Dear High Commissioner’ or ‘Dear Ambassador’.

rules.specification: Treat the informal openings as recipient-specific. Do not assess informal openings to nuncios: the page gives no informal salutation for that role.
rules.violation_condition: Formal correspondence to an ambassador, high commissioner or nuncio lacks the opening ‘Your Excellency’, or informal correspondence to a high commissioner or ambassador lacks the corresponding opening ‘Dear High Commissioner’ or ‘Dear Ambassador’.
when: Applies to emails and letters.
Formal correspondence to ambassadors, high commissioners and nuncios opens with ‘Your Excellency’.
Informal correspondence to high commissioners opens with ‘Dear High Commissioner’.
Informal correspondence to ambassadors opens with ‘Dear Ambassador’.
rules.why: G-2 combines formal and informal cases into one salutation check; the closing formula is a separate property of the correspondence.

covers.quote: In formal correspondence with ambassadors, high commissioners and nuncios:
In informal correspondence:
Conclude with ‘Yours sincerely’.

rules.violation_condition: Correspondence to an ambassador, high commissioner or nuncio lacks ‘Yours faithfully’ as its formal closing formula, or lacks ‘Yours sincerely’ as its informal closing formula.
when: Applies to emails and letters to ambassadors, high commissioners and nuncios.
Formal correspondence concludes with ‘Yours faithfully’.
Informal correspondence concludes with ‘Yours sincerely’.
rules.why: G-2 combines formal and informal cases into one closing-formula check, separate from the opening salutation.

covers.quote: Use the name and official position to address:
diplomatic staff (such as chargés d’affaires and counsellors)
consular appointees (such as consuls general, vice-consuls and honorary consuls).

parts.quote: Ms Susan Grace, Consul General in Chennai

rules.quote: Address other diplomatic staff by name and appointment
rules.violation_condition: An address for other diplomatic staff or a consular appointee omits the person’s name or official position.
when: Applies to diplomatic staff such as chargés d’affaires and counsellors.
Also applies to consular appointees such as consuls general, vice-consuls and honorary consuls.
rules.why: G-4 absorbs the body restatement; G-2 keeps the diplomatic and consular recipient categories within one name-and-position check.
